14A.
Council initiated item from Mayor Bruce Ehlers regarding preservation of mobile home parks in Encinitas as a naturally occurring affordable housing solution.
Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines because it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment. The action is also exempt from CEQA under Section 15378(b)(5) of the CEQA Guidelines because it involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
Recommended questions and associated actions for staff:
1. Can Encinitas enact a moratorium on mobile home space rent increases that would retroactively set rents at January 1, 2026, rates until a future permanent "rent fairness ordinance" could be adopted? What options do we have and what are their ramifications?
2. Is it possible to adopt the moratorium using an urgency ordinance?
3. Compile a list of all Mobile Home Parks in Encinitas. Provide details such as number of rented spaces, zoning, applicable specific plan policies, existing lease escalation terms (if any) and ownership parties of the underlying land. Some parks are in zones specific to Mobile Home Parks and others are in Rural Residential. The analysis should include a description of the various zones and the resulting protection or lack of protections for mobile home parks.
4. What are the requirements for notification and due process that the City must follow so that all parties are notified and given ample legal notice? Is there an approximate resulting timeline?
5. Provide a recommended approach (not formal ordinance language) for a rent fairness ordinance and provide evaluation of similar ordinances that have been implemented elsewhere in CA (such as in Fortuna, CA).
Staff would be directed to investigate these questions and any others that the Council desires answered. Staff would return at a future meeting, preferably urgently, to have Council consider an ordinance and other actions such as an ordinance and/or moratorium.

Council initiated item from Deputy Mayor Jim O'Hara regarding discussing any action being taken by staff and action needed to address and take advantage of Governor Newsom's statewide Emergency proclamation, and to additionally bring staff related sand replenishment actions and reports directly to the City Manager's office to expedite decisions around sand replenishment and the Governor's proclamation.
Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines because it can be seen with certainty that there is no possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment. Discuss, providing direction to staff to evaluate and develop a proactive sand replenishment and erosion mitigation plan, to align with Governor Newsom's Emergency Proclamation for a potentially record-breaking El Niño winter.
Discuss directing staff to address the following:
1. Report Current Beach Conditions
2. Explore Sand Replenishment Options
3. Implement Temporary Protective Measures
4. Coordinate with State & Regional Partners
5. Communicate the Developed Public Communication & Preparedness Plan
6. Funding Strategy
Report back by November 15, 2026, with findings and a recommended action plan

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
